description: Make a whole matching game art set in the game's CAMERA VIEW: characters, props and tiles drawn on 2048 GPT-Image 2.6 sheets, cut into one asset per item, each tagged with the view's dimension and facing so rotate_sprite and the animation tools use the right angle. view: 'platformer' (side profile facing right, eye level), 'topdown' (classic RPG, ~45° camera, characters head-on and symmetrical), 'topdown-overhead' (straight down), 'isometric'. Items are planned onto sheets (about 3-4 characters, 4-6 objects or 3 tall props a sheet; the first sheet, or style_asset_id, is the style every later sheet copies at full resolution). Cost: 20 a sheet + 10 a cut; pass estimate_only to see the plan and price first. Every piece gets a free view check (head-on for top-down, a profile for platformer) and failures are reported with a redraw offer; nothing else is spent (no rotations or animations). Voidless+ only. Returns set_id: add_to_asset_set adds to it later. Every piece gets a world_height in heights of the set's reference character (the first humanoid, or the item marked reference), measured on the sheet before the cut-outs are reframed, or the item's own `size` when given. In a game, size every piece from world_height and the export's scale data (export_godot_spriteframes with asset_id), never by guessing from the image size: all cut-outs are framed to the same pixel height.

estimate_only.description: true = only the sheet plan and the price; nothing is drawn or charged

items.description: Everything the set needs, e.g. [{name:'knight'}, {name:'frost wolf', body:'quadruped'}]

body.description: Characters: body plan (a wolf is quadruped, a slime blob, a bat flying). Omitted: guessed

kind.description: character (rotated and animated), object (a prop) or tile. Omitted: guessed from the name

name.description: What it is, e.g. 'knight', 'ice golem', 'treasure chest'

notes.description: Optional details: colours, outfit, what it holds

reference.description: This item is the set's unit of height (default: the first humanoid character)

shape.description: Optional: how it fits a cell (a tree is tall, a cart wide). Omitted: guessed

size.description: Its height in the game world, as a multiple of the set's reference character (the hero = 1): a boss golem 2.5, a slime 0.5, a door 1.2. Wins over the height the sheet draws (sheets often draw a boss barely bigger than the hero). Give it whenever relative size matters

style.description: Style preset (smooth styles: cartoon, cel-shading, flat, hand-drawn, anime, watercolor, comic-book, 3d-render, ...). Not pixel art: resize_sprite the pieces afterwards

style_asset_id.description: Optional: an existing sheet (or any image asset) whose style the whole set copies, at full resolution

style_words.description: Optional extra style words for every sheet, e.g. 'muted colours, matte shading, medium outlines'

name: generate_asset_set
